candidates.name: fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for FRED/ALFRED. Explicitly supports point-in-time / vintage pulls via get_series_as_of_date() and get_series_all_releases(), using realtime_start/realtime_end params to reconstruct 'what was known when' for any FRED series (CPI, GDP, consumer confidence, etc). Apache 2.0, 67 commits, actively maintained (workflow runs through Oct 2024).
candidates.why_useful: Directly implements gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages). Would let us pull point-in-time versions of the ~40 FRED series (CPI lodging, airfares) and BEA/consumer-confidence-adjacent series already in the CONTEXT inventory, so every macro input to the model can be refit at the guide date rather than using today's revised values (the CLAUDE.md point-in-time rule).
candidates.last_activity: workflow/CI activity through 2024, repo actively maintained
candidates.time_coverage: Full ALFRED vintage history per series (varies by series, many back to 1990s)

candidates.name: alfred (R package)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (on CRAN) with get_alfred_series() and get_fred_series(): downloads ALFRED vintage data by observation-date and realtime-date range, returns tidy data.frame, no API key required. MIT licensed, 20 stars, last updated 2021-07-26, actively usable.
candidates.why_useful: A no-key alternative/cross-check to fredapi for pulling point-in-time macro vintages (gap #4); useful if the team's Python fredapi key setup is inconvenient or for R-based backtest scripts.

candidates.name: fredr
candidates.what_it_holds: R bindings to the FRED API; example calls return realtime_start/realtime_end columns confirming ALFRED vintage support. 101 stars, 242 commits, MIT-style license, active (recent examples dated 2021+, CI enabled).
candidates.why_useful: Another mature, well-maintained R client covering the same point-in-time macro-vintage need as fredapi/alfred (gap #4); wider adoption (101 stars) than onnokleen/alfred so likely more battle-tested for edge cases.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with onnokleen/alfred and fredapi in function

candidates.name: fedfred
candidates.what_it_holds: Feature-rich Python package covering FRED, GeoFRED, ALFRED, and FRASER APIs; native Pandas/Polars/Dask support, async requests, local caching, rate limiting. MIT licensed, 359 commits, v3.0.0, 9 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Newer/broader alternative to fredapi with explicit ALFRED support plus GeoFRED (regional/state series, useful for the STR-regulation and regional-macro gaps) and caching for repeated point-in-time backtests.

candidates.name: fbi (Factor-Based Imputation)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package implementing factor-based imputation for FRED-MD/FRED-QD style monthly/quarterly macro panels (McCracken & Ng 2015/2016 databases); does not bundle the data itself but provides loader/imputation functions and a vignette using FRED-MD. GPL-3.0.
candidates.why_useful: Useful methods layer if the team pulls the (separately hosted) FRED-MD/FRED-QD standardized macro panels and needs missing-value handling consistent with the academic real-time-data literature; adjacent to point-in-time macro nowcasting methods (gap #17).

candidates.name: FRBNY Nowcasting (Bok et al. NY Fed Staff Nowcast replication)
candidates.what_it_holds: Official replication code (MATLAB) for the paper 'Macroeconomic Nowcasting and Forecasting with Big Data' (NY Fed Staff Reports). Includes example US data pulled from FRED (data/ folder), a model spec file (Spec_US_example.xls), and a pre-computed dynamic factor model result (ResDFM.mat). BSD-3-Clause, 4 commits on master, low activity but stable/canonical.
candidates.why_useful: The canonical open-source dynamic-factor-model nowcasting framework built around mixed-frequency, real-time-vintage macro inputs -- directly the kind of 'methods: nowcasting with mixed-frequency data (MIDAS, DFM)' tooling named in gap #17, and a template for how to structure our own quarterly nowcast around vintage macro releases.
candidates.last_activity: low (4 commits), but canonical/stable reference implementation
candidates.time_coverage: example vintage from paper era; not full historical ALFRED archive
candidates.size_hint: small (spec + example data files, MATLAB scripts)

candidates.name: gtab (Google Trends Anchor Bank)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package/CLI (pip-installable) implementing 'gtab': builds a calibrated anchor bank of pre-computed queries so that repeated/independent Google Trends pulls return comparable absolute values instead of the API's rounded, 5-term-relative output. Requires building a time/geography-specific anchor bank. MIT licensed, 217 commits, 123 stars, 25 forks.
candidates.why_useful: Directly named in CONTEXT gap #17 ('anchored Google Trends (gtab)'). CONTEXT notes raw Google Trends as pulled failed (0/162, renormalisation issues) -- gtab is the specific fix for that renormalisation problem via calibrated anchor banks, and per-anchor-bank timeframes make historical pulls closer to point-in-time reproducible, which is squarely this theme's remit (vintage-aware, reproducible macro/search-interest series).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Google Trends (9 terms) already held but explicitly NOT point-in-time and already found not to work as pulled; gtab is a different, untested construction
candidates.time_coverage: user-defined anchor bank windows, any historical period Trends covers
candidates.size_hint: library + CLI, anchor banks generated on demand (not bundled)

candidates.name: RJDemetra / JDemetra+
candidates.what_it_holds: R interface (and underlying Java app at github.com/jdemetra) to JDemetra+, the seasonal-adjustment software officially recommended to Eurostat's European Statistical System and the ESCB since 2015. Implements TRAMO/SEATS, X-13ARIMA-SEATS, plus nowcasting, temporal disaggregation, and benchmarking utilities. EUPL-1.2, 503 commits, 55 stars.
candidates.why_useful: This is literally the tool that produces the ONS/Eurostat seasonally-adjusted series and revisions we're trying to reason about; useful if we need to re-run or understand how Eurostat's tour_ce_omr platform-nights series (already held) gets seasonally adjusted/revised, or to build our own vintage-consistent seasonal adjustment of any series we pull point-in-time.

candidates.name: peruvian_gdp_revisions (Peru Real-Time GDP dataset pipeline)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python pipeline (scrape -> OCR for pre-2013 scans -> clean -> vintage-format / releases-format output) that reconstructs a real-time GDP vintage dataset for Peru from BCRP Weekly Reports, 1994-2025 (monthly and quarterly/annual). Actual processed vintage CSV/Parquet outputs are hosted on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18099975); GitHub repo (MIT, 1,289 commits, 1 star) holds only the code. Includes OCR for scanned pre-2013 PDFs.
candidates.why_useful: A genuine, working real-time/vintage GDP dataset construction for a LatAm economy (gap #7 regional travel/macro outside US/EU is adjacent; more directly this is a template + actual vintage dataset for point-in-time macro data outside the US ALFRED system, filling the 'ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages... elsewhere' spirit of this theme for a market ABNB reports LatAm revenue in).
candidates.size_hint: dataset hosted externally on Zenodo; pipeline code in repo

candidates.name: public-market-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Small but functional Python/Airflow/Postgres pipeline that ingests FRED data (currently just one JSON endpoint implemented; BCB/SEC EDGAR planned) while preserving three timestamps per observation (reference date, publication date, collection date), explicitly 'so backtests never see a future revision.' MIT, 6 commits, 12 tests/92% coverage, 0 stars -- very new/small project.
candidates.why_useful: A working minimal reference implementation of exactly the point-in-time ingestion discipline the CLAUDE.md rule #2 demands (vendor + timestamp per value); could be read as a design pattern even if not adopted wholesale, though it's early-stage and only covers one FRED endpoint so far.

candidates.name: RevisionLedger
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python bitemporal-ledger library (valid time + system/knowledge time per data point) demonstrated on ALFRED's Real GDP series (GDPC1), with two real sample vintages of Q4-2023 US real GDP committed as fixtures with SHA-256 manifests. 16 passing tests, MIT, 0 stars, 14 commits -- proof-of-concept scope, explicitly not a general downloader yet.
candidates.why_useful: A tiny, clean reference implementation of 'as-of' querying for macro vintages (exactly this theme), but scope is currently limited to a worked example, not a usable general tool yet.
candidates.time_coverage: single worked example (Q4 2023 GDP, two vintages)

candidates.name: vintage (as-of statistics query tool)
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-file Python/SQLite CLI tool (vintage.py) that ingests generic CSV releases (series_id, period, released_at, value) and supports 'as-of' snapshots and 'diff' comparisons between two knowledge dates; preserves source text so trivial revisions (1.0 -> 1.00) aren't lost. MIT, 1 commit, 0 stars -- generic, source-agnostic, user must supply their own release CSVs (no bundled data).
candidates.why_useful: Generic point-in-time query tool that could sit on top of any macro series the team already scrapes with a release timestamp (e.g. consensus snapshots, FRED pulls) to do as-of queries without building custom code; very early/minimal though.

candidates.name: pandaSDMX
candidates.what_it_holds: Python SDMX 2.1 client for pulling statistical data/metadata directly from Eurostat, ECB, ONS, World Bank, and other SDMX-compliant providers into pandas objects. Apache 2.0, 928 commits, 134 stars, actively maintained with CI across multiple doc versions.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose acquisition method for Eurostat/ONS series beyond what's already held (tour_ce_omr platform nights); does not itself expose vintages/revisions explicitly, but is the standard way to programmatically pull ONS/Eurostat series (including revision-relevant series like GDP, consumer spend, tourism) for building our own vintage archive going forward by re-pulling on a schedule.

candidates.name: eurostat (R package)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package for searching, downloading, and manipulating Eurostat open data; example query for air passenger transport returns data spanning 1993-2026. 1,433 commits, actively maintained (v4.1.0.9008), EU grant-funded.
candidates.why_useful: Mature, well-maintained alternative acquisition path for Eurostat series (including tourism/travel and consumer indicators) beyond the single tour_ce_omr series already held; does not appear to expose vintages/revisions explicitly but is a solid pull tool for expanding Eurostat coverage.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with existing Eurostat tour_ce_omr pull; this is a general-purpose client, not vintage-specific
candidates.license: not fully specified in fetch (LICENSE file present)
candidates.time_coverage: varies by series, e.g. 1993-2026 for air transport example

notes: This session's shared WebSearch tool budget (200/session, apparently pooled across all concurrently running scout subagents) was already exhausted before this scout's first query, so WebSearch was unusable for the entire run -- every candidate here was found via WebFetch against github.com/topics/<tag> pages (which worked reliably) and direct repo-URL guesses from domain knowledge (which mostly resolved). github.com/search?q=... consistently returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) on every attempt; grep.app also 429'd. DuckDuckGo HTML search served a CAPTCHA wall; Bing search via WebFetch returned garbage/irrelevant cached results (likely JS-rendered page not captured by the fetcher), so neither was usable as a WebSearch substitute. Recommendation for whoever runs another web-modality scout on a similar theme: rely on github.com/topics/<tag> browsing plus targeted repo-URL fetches rather than github.com/search or third-party search engines, since those paths were the only ones that worked here. Notable dead ends: no repos found for ONS-API python/R clients specifically, no repos tagged 'real-time-data-set' or 'economic-data-revisions' or 'vintage-data'-adjacent Eurostat/ONS-specific projects beyond the small generic vintage-ledger tools listed above (RevisionLedger, vintage, public-market-data) which are all very new (0-1 stars, <20 commits, created ~2026) and narrow in scope -- worth a re-check in a few months if they mature, but not worth over-weighting today. Philadelphia Fed's actual 'Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists' does not appear to have any GitHub-hosted mirror, replication package, or client library findable through the paths available to this scout (its raw .xls files are typically pulled directly from the Philly Fed website, not GitHub) -- this specific named target of the brief came up empty. Consensus-estimate vintage / historical analyst-estimate-history repos (also part of gap #4) were not found either; that sub-target may need a different search modality (e.g. gh code search, which this modality was told not to use).
